$comment: Accepted npm audit advisories. Every entry is a deliberate, dated decision,
not a mute. The audit gate fails on any critical or high advisory that is NOT
listed here, fails on any entry past its expiry, and fails on any entry that no
longer matches a real advisory — so this file cannot quietly outlive its reasons.
Why these exist: npm reports a 'fix available' for every entry below, and in
each case that fix is a MAJOR DOWNGRADE, not an upgrade. npm audit fix --force
would take Next 16.2.11 to 9.3.3 and Trigger.dev 4.5.7 to 1.0.8 — rolling the
application back roughly five years to satisfy a scanner. That is a worse
outcome than the advisories themselves. The real fix is upstream: these are
transitive dependencies pinned by Next.js and Trigger.dev, and they resolve when
those packages update, not when we act.
Before adding an entry, confirm three things: the advisory is genuinely
unfixable without a destructive change, the exposure is understood and written
in 'reason', and an expiry is set. An entry with a vague reason is a mute
Reviewed 2026-07-28. Tracked as OBL-03 in docs/plans/OPEN_OBLIGATIONS.md.

exceptions.reason: Arbitrary file creation/overwrite. Reached only through the trigger.dev CLI's dev-time package extraction. Not present in the production dependency tree, so it does not ship and is not reachable by the deployed application. npm's only fix is trigger.dev@1.0.8, a downgrade from 4.5.7.

Production framework. npm's proposed fix is next@9.3.3, a downgrade of seven major versions from 16.2.11 that would break the entire application. Current version is recent; resolve by tracking upstream Next releases rather than rolling back.

XSS via unescaped </style>. Transitive through Next.js, which pins the version; the offered fix is the next@9.3.3 downgrade. Exposure is limited to build-time CSS processing of first-party stylesheets, not user-supplied content.
Inherited libvips vulnerabilities. Transitive through Next.js image optimisation and pinned by it. This application serves no user-uploaded images; the image surface is first-party static assets.
Transitive through @trigger.dev/sdk and pinned by it. npm's fix is @trigger.dev/sdk@3.3.17, a major downgrade from 4.5.7. Resolves when Trigger.dev publishes an updated core.

Uninitialised memory disclosure. Reached through the Trigger.dev realtime transport and pinned by it. The application does not expose a WebSocket server to untrusted clients; the connection is outbound to Trigger.dev.
Polling transport crash. Same transport chain as ws, pinned by Trigger.dev. Outbound client connection only; no inbound Socket.IO server is exposed by this application.
Same Trigger.dev realtime transport chain as ws and engine.io. Client-side use only.
Linting toolchain. Does not ship. The offered fix chain runs through eslint-config-next@12.0.4, a downgrade from 16.2.11 that would break Next.js linting.
Linting toolchain, does not ship. Proposed fix is a downgrade to 12.0.4 from 16.2.11, which would decouple linting from the installed Next.js major.
